state.context: The HTTP catalogue in Can exposes opaque immutable response values and requires awaiting a named handler completely before one native Response conversion. Its contract has no rule making those values single-use, while a native body can be consumed. Routing supports only exact static GET/POST paths, decoded after native URL normalization, with HEAD never supplied automatically and capture/wildcard matching absent. Both duplicate_route(method,path) and ambiguous_route(first,second) are declared. Distinct authored spellings may produce an identical decoded normalized path. Existing consumers impose no compatibility obligations. Select internal storage and collision policy without adding catalogue APIs.

response.instructions: Choose the response storage/conversion behavior most consistent with the supplied contract.

criteria.snapshot: Represent the value by private immutable status/header/body data; make one new native Response per finished handler invocation so value reuse remains valid.
criteria.consume: Attach mutable used-state to the opaque value and reject reuse after the first request has converted it.
criteria.cache: Store a single constructed native Response and return that shared instance on every request using the value.

routes.instructions: Select the treatment of normalization aliases that best fits the stated router contracts.

criteria.collision: Use the ingress normalizer on valid route literals; same-method repeated literals cause duplicate_route, whereas different literals with one normalized destination cause ambiguous_route; distinct GET/POST registrations coexist.
criteria.strict: Demand the canonical decoded path as the only permitted literal, reporting invalid_route for aliases before router creation can see a collision.
criteria.overwrite: Resolve multiple spellings targeting the same method/path by replacing earlier entries with later ones.
